```{r}
# Every live number on this page comes from _metrics.R — never hand-write them.
source("_metrics.R")

sch <- metrics_scholar()

cites_display    <- fmt_floor(sch$total_cites, 100)
h_display        <- if (is.na(sch$h_index)) "—" else as.character(sch$h_index)
cites5_display   <- fmt_floor(metrics_recent_cites(sch), 100)
flagship_display <- fmt_floor(sch$flagship_cites, 100)
bibl_display     <- fmt_floor(metrics_cran_total("bibliometrix"), 10000)
```

<span class="eyebrow">Profile · Massimo Aria</span>

<p class="lede">Full Professor in Statistics for Social Sciences at the Department of Economics and Statistics of the University of Naples Federico II. Ph.D. in Computational Statistics.</p>

::: {.dropcap}
For more than twenty years I have taught Statistics and Machine Learning across bachelor's, master's, and doctoral programmes. Courses I currently teach include **Statistics for Social Sciences**, **Advanced Statistical Methods for Social Research**, **Sampling Surveys**, and the **Lab of Machine Learning in R**.
:::

My main research fields include **bibliometrics**, **science mapping**, **systematic literature reviews**, **statistical survey methodology**, **machine learning**, and **text mining**. I have led numerous statistical surveys and data-science projects related to economic, social, ethological, and healthcare phenomena.

---

## Scientific Activities

I have authored more than **200 peer-reviewed scientific articles**, of which **38** have been classified as "A" (top tier) in scientific area 13 (Economics and Statistics) by **ANVUR** (Italian Agency of University Research Evaluation).

I am the co-founder of the <a href="https://www.k-synth.com" target="_blank">**K-Synth Academic Spin-off**</a>, a science-centric information and intelligence start-up focused on the extraction and analysis of knowledge from large volumes of heterogeneous data through quantitative, statistical, and data-science methods.

I am the Scientific Coordinator of the <a href="https://bibliometrix.org/sssm/" target="_blank">**Summer School in Science Mapping (SSSM)**</a> and a faculty member of the <a href="https://esss.info/" target="_blank">**European Summer School of Scientometrics (ESSS)**</a>.

---

## Academic and Institutional Roles

- Board member of the **Naples Ph.D. Program in Economics**
- Board member for over 20 years of the **Ph.D. programs in Computational Statistics** and **Social Sciences and Statistics**
- Since 2019, board member of the **Master's degree in Data Science** and in **Economics** (curriculum: *Data Scientist for Economics*)
- Since 2010, I have coordinated — together with Prof. C. Cuccurullo — the research group in **bibliometrics and science mapping** at the University of Naples Federico II and the University of Campania L. Vanvitelli ([www.bibliometrix.org](https://www.bibliometrix.org))
- I have coordinated or participated in **5 European projects**, **3 PNRR projects**, **5 PRIN projects**, **1 FIRB project**, and **11 national or regional projects**
- Since 2007, scientific committee member of the **Statistical Algorithms and Software Specialized Team**, ERCIM Working Group on Computational and Methodological Statistics
- Currently responsible for the **Research Quality Assessment (VQR)** of the Department of Economics and Statistics

---

## Scientific Results and Awards

To date, my publications have received **over `r cites_display` citations**, and my **H-index is `r h_display`**. In the last five years alone, my publications have been cited more than **`r cites5_display` times** (source: Google Scholar).

My article *"bibliometrix: An R-tool for comprehensive science mapping analysis"* (2017, *Journal of Informetrics*, IF 5.107) is:

- The **most-cited article ever** in the journal — `r flagship_display`+ citations on Google Scholar
- One of the **top-downloaded** articles on ScienceDirect ([source](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1751157717300500))

---

## Social Impact of My Research Activities

**Bibliometrix** and its Shiny web-app **Biblioshiny** are recognised as the most comprehensive and user-friendly software for science mapping. In a widely cited review of bibliometric tools, Moral-Muñoz et al. (2020) wrote:

> At this moment, maybe Bibliometrix and its Shiny platform contain the more extensive set of techniques implemented, and together with the easiness of its interface, could be a great software for practitioners.

Today, Bibliometrix is one of the **most used** science-mapping tools worldwide, with:

- **`r bibl_display`+** installations
- A **large international community** of researchers actively using and promoting it
- **Over 200 YouTube tutorials** in multiple languages

In the past four years I have delivered **over 60 seminars** in Italian doctoral schools (Universities of Bergamo, Brescia, Calabria, Genoa, Polytechnic of Milan, Naples, Pisa, Rome, Salento, Turin, among others) and international ones (Universities of Bodø — Norway, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Granada, London, Melbourne, Paris, and the NOVA Information Management School in Lisbon).
